items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: And this Hans Buerman come up and says I'm glad you didn't say nothing, Jacques. I couldn't have helped you.

ctx.x: So, I said well -- I went there that next day and there was a woman protesting about her son. They took her son away and I said, well, I don't know nothing and she was saying who was no good and everybody so -- all of a sudden four soldiers come and grabbed the woman and took her out.
And this Hans Buerman come up and says I'm glad you didn't say nothing, Jacques. I couldn't have helped you.
And I say, well, I don't know nothing. I didn't have nothing to say and I stayed there. The British were bombing. The British were taking care of business. They were bombing and bombing and bombing.
